newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CAR DEALERS UP 1997 SALES FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CAR DEALERS UP 1997 SALES FORECAST.

text.p: Finnish car dealers have upgraded their forecast for 1997 new private car sales to 110,000 from their November forecast of 102,000, the Information Centre of the Automobile Branch said in a statement received on Wednesday.
In 1996, registrations of new private cars increased 20 percent year-on-year to 95,830 units, it said.

"The increase in new private car sales is expected to continue during 1997," it said. "If the (Finnish) economy develops as expected, it is regarded as possible to reach sales of 110,000 new private cars," the centre said, adding that would be an increase of 15 percent over 1996.
Annual new private car registrations in Finland peaked at nearly 180,000 in 1988-89, but fell sharply as recession set in early in the 1990s. In 1993, new private car sales fell below 60,000 units.
Finnish car dealers expect sales of vans to rise to about
11,500 in 1997 from 8,883 in 1996 while lorry sales would remain
unchanged around 3,700 (3,733 in 1996), the centre said.
